citation: Scharinger, Christian, Yvonne Kammerer, and Peter Gerjets. "Pupil Dilation and EEG Alpha Frequency Band Power Reveal Load on Executive Functions for Link-Selection Processes during Text Reading." PLoS ONE 10, no. 6 (2015): e0130608. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0130608. [NOTE: the provisional header supplied for this unit listed the year as 2019; the article's own citation line, running head, and DOI confirm publication as 2015 (received 27 Dec 2014, accepted 21 May 2015, published 15 June 2015). The enclosing folder name retains "(2019)" only because that exact string was specified in this unit's output-path instruction; flagged for correction in the cluster manifest.]
discipline: cognitive psychology / psychophysiology of reading and hypertext, designing and testing a dual-modality (pupillometry + EEG alpha) methodology for executive-function load during hyperlink-like selection
thesis: Scharinger, Kammerer, and Gerjets isolate the load contributed by the initial hyperlink-like link-selection decision itself, distinct from the load of navigating and integrating subsequent web pages, and directly compare two physiological load-measures, pupil dilation and EEG alpha frequency band power, within the same reading task -- a comparison not previously attempted in either constrained working-memory paradigms or unconstrained hypertext reading. Across three experiments, participants read a standardized German reading-comprehension text (the LGVT) containing embedded three-word bracketed decision points simulating hyperlink selection, while pupil diameter (250 Hz SMI eye-tracker) and 27-channel EEG were recorded concurrently. Experiment 1 (N=23) establishes that both pupil dilation increases and EEG alpha power (8-13 Hz, electrode Pz) decreases during link-selection relative to pure-reading baseline epochs. Experiment 2 (N=19 analyzed) replicates this after removing perceptual (word color) and motor (mouse-click) confounds. Experiment 3 (N=24, pupil-only) shows no difference once a structural/difficulty confound is also removed, confirming the earlier effects were load-related. Contrary to expectation, however, the two physiological measures never correlate with one another across experiments, even though each independently tracks the load manipulation -- the paper's central, unresolved empirical puzzle. This source contains no mention of boredom anywhere in its text; it is a purely cognitive-load / executive-function study relevant to this cluster only through its dual-measure (pupillometry + EEG alpha) methodology and its analogical bearing on attention/engagement constructs.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.summary: States the gap (no prior direct comparison of pupil dilation and EEG alpha as load measures within one reading task), previews the three-experiment dual-modality methodology, and reports the central surprising non-correlation between the two load-measures despite both independently showing the predicted effect.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Defines executive functions (EFs: updating, shifting, inhibition, citing Miyake et al.); reviews Kintsch's construction-integration model of text comprehension, distinguishing a construction step (affected by link-selection) from an integration step (affected by subsequent pages); reviews the one directly comparable prior study (Fitzsimmons, Weal & Drieghe) finding no overall disruption effect from non-clickable hyperlinks; reviews pupil-dilation load literature (Kahneman & Beatty; Laeng et al.'s locus-coeruleus/arousal account; Di Stasi et al.'s hypermedia pupillometry study finding limited sensitivity to subjective difficulty) and EEG-alpha load literature (event-related desynchronization, Pfurtscheller & Lopes da Silva; Klimesch's attention/inhibitory-control account; Antonenko & Niederhauser's hypertext-leads alpha study); states three hypotheses (1a: pupil dilation increases in the test condition; 1b: alpha power decreases; 2: the two difference-scores correlate negatively).

sections.title: Experiment 1 -- Methods, Results, Discussion
sections.summary: N=23 university students; LGVT reading-comprehension text (1,727 words) with 23 embedded three-word bracketed decision points; SMI 250 Hz eye-tracker; 27-electrode EEG (10/20 system, 500 Hz); 2-second epochs. Confirms Hypotheses 1a and 1b (pupil dilation up, alpha power down during link-selection); a 3-way hemisphere x electrode-site x condition ANOVA shows left-lateralized, parietal-occipital-maximal alpha effects; Hypothesis 2 disconfirmed (no pupil/alpha correlation); alpha-power change correlates negatively (marginal) with LGVT comprehension score. Discussion flags perceptual (word-color) and motor (mouse-click) confounds as alternative explanations.

sections.title: Experiment 2 -- Methods, Results, Discussion
sections.summary: Modifies the baseline condition to require a matched mouse-click and removes the color cue used for links, controlling perceptual/motor confounds. N=20 recruited, 19 analyzed after one exclusion. Replicates Experiment 1's pupil-dilation and alpha-power effects and the null pupil/alpha correlation; the negative alpha-comprehension correlation becomes statistically significant (p<.05).

sections.title: Experiment 3 -- Methods, Results and Discussion
sections.summary: Equalizes test and baseline task structure (single word only, no distractor selection) to rule out a sentence-difficulty confound. N=24; pupil-dilation-only design (EEG omitted for efficiency). No difference in pupil dilation between conditions, as predicted, confirming the Experiment 1-2 effects were not structural artifacts.

sections.title: General Discussion
sections.summary: Synthesizes across experiments; both physiological measures are sensitive to EF load during hyperlink-like selection. Offers two non-adjudicated accounts of the persistent pupil/alpha non-correlation: differential sensitivity to distinct load aspects (cognitive vs. motivational/emotional/arousal), or individual differences in which measure is more sensitive per participant. Discusses ecological-validity limitations (non-functional links, forced linear reading, repeated same-position link sequences); situates the work within 'neuro-ergonomics'; proposes future differential-EF-loading manipulations and more naturalistic hypertext materials.

sections.title: Supporting information / Author contributions / References
sections.summary: Three supplementary data tables (raw alpha-power and pupil-dilation data per experiment); author contributions; 85 references drawn entirely from cognitive-psychology, psychophysiology, and hypertext/HCI literatures -- no boredom-specific citations.

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: analogical only -- not the source's own vocabulary. The paper's 'inhibition' EF, defined as general processes of interference control/executive attention, names the same control-failure mechanism that boredom researchers elsewhere in this cluster invoke for attentional disengagement, but Scharinger et al. study intact, effortfully deployed inhibition during a structured task, not its breakdown.

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: analogical only. The task is deliberately calibrated so participants are 'neither over- nor under-loaded,' with comprehension scores in the 'upper third' of standardized norms -- an empirical portrait of bounded, effortful task engagement, though the authors never use engagement/flow vocabulary.

constructs.label: mind-wandering / task-unrelated thought
constructs.treatment: analogical only. The same EF-inhibition mechanism (suppressing distractor words during selection) is the executive-control substrate that resource-control models of mind-wandering invoke for failures to suppress task-unrelated thought, though this paper never engages that literature or names mind-wandering.

measures.label: pupil dilation / pupillometry
measures.signal: pupil diameter (mm), averaged left/right eye, per 2-second epoch
measures.apparatus: 250 Hz SMI (SensoMotoric Instruments) infrared remote eye-tracker; 22-inch Dell monitor, 1680x1050 px; chin rest, ~70 cm eye-to-screen distance; 9-point SMI Experiment Center calibration; SMI iView X 2.7.13 software
measures.sampleN: Exp.1 N=23; Exp.2 N=19 analyzed (of 20 recruited); Exp.3 N=24
measures.keyResult: increased in test (link-selection) vs. baseline condition in Exp.1 (3.58mm vs 3.51mm, F(1,22)=21.85, p<.001, np2=.50) and Exp.2 (3.64mm vs 3.57mm, F(1,18)=32.61, p<.001, np2=.64); no difference in Exp.3 once selection difficulty was equalized (3.67mm vs 3.66mm, F(1,23)=.04, p=.85), ruling out a structural confound; never correlated with EEG alpha-power change (Exp.1 r=-.16 ns; Exp.2 r=-.14 ns)

measures.label: EEG alpha/theta power
measures.signal: EEG alpha frequency band power (8-13 Hz), FFT over 2-second epochs, primary analysis at electrode Pz plus a 3-way hemisphere x electrode-site topographic analysis; theta band not analyzed
measures.apparatus: 27 scalp electrodes (Fp1,Fp2,F7,F3,Fz,F4,F8,FC5,FC1,FC2,FC6,T7,C3,Cz,C4,T8,CP5,CP1,CP2,CP6,P7,P3,Pz,P4,P8,O1,O2; 10/20 system), right-mastoid reference, AFz ground, 3 EOG electrodes; PyCorder/ActiCHamp (Brainproducts), 500 Hz, active ActiCap electrodes, impedance <5kOhm; 0.5-40Hz FIR filtering, ICA-based EOG correction, average re-reference, +-100uV artifact rejection
measures.keyResult: decreased in test vs. baseline at Pz in Exp.1 (6.58 vs 7.96 uV2/Hz, F(1,22)=16.05, p=.001, np2=.42) and Exp.2 (8.05 vs 8.87 uV2/Hz, F(1,18)=15.00, p=.001, np2=.45); left-lateralized, parietal-occipital-maximal (3-way ANOVA interactions, both experiments); negatively correlated with LGVT reading-comprehension score (Exp.1 r=-.41 marginal p<.10; Exp.2 r=-.50, p<.05); never correlated with pupil-dilation change

measures.label: gaze variance / fixation dispersion
measures.signal: binocular gaze position used to define text-line areas of interest (AOIs) for epoch placement, and visually inspected for reading-pattern regularity
measures.apparatus: same SMI 250Hz eye-tracker as the pupillometry channel
measures.treatment: secondary/apparatus use only -- not itself a reported dependent measure or statistic; used to confirm a generally linear (non-skimming) reading process with only brief back-and-forth jumps near decision points
measures.keyResult: no quantified gaze-dispersion result reported; qualitative confirmation of linear reading pattern only

measures.label: blink / eye-closure
measures.signal: eye-blink artifacts (missing data points) in the continuous eye-tracking stream
measures.treatment: corrected via linear interpolation during preprocessing only; not analyzed as a dependent measure
measures.keyResult: no blink-rate or eye-closure finding reported

measures.label: behavioral (RT / errors / performance-monitoring)
measures.signal: LGVT reading-comprehension score (+2 per correctly selected word, -1 per incorrectly selected word) and total reading time (minutes)
measures.apparatus: LGVT (Lesegeschwindigkeits- und -Verstaendnistest), a standardized German reading-comprehension instrument, scored per its published manual
measures.sampleN: Exp.1 N=23; Exp.2 N=19; Exp.3 N=24 (reading time only)
measures.keyResult: comprehension score negatively correlated with alpha-power change (Exp.1 r=-.41 marginal; Exp.2 r=-.50 p<.05) and strongly with reading time (Exp.1 r=-.80 p<.001; Exp.2 r=-.84 p<.001); not correlated with pupil-dilation change in either experiment

measures.label: EEG frontal alpha asymmetry
measures.signal: not operationalized as the classic frontal (F3/F4) approach-withdrawal asymmetry index
measures.treatment: the reported hemisphere/electrode-site laterality effects are topographic (left-hemisphere, parietal-occipital-maximal decrease) tied to linguistic-task lateralization, a distinct construct from classic frontal alpha asymmetry; flagged here to prevent conflation, not because the source treats the construct

readings.claim: Pupil dilation increased significantly in the test (link-selection) condition versus baseline in both Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, confirming Hypothesis 1a.

EEG alpha frequency band power at electrode Pz decreased significantly in the test condition versus baseline in both Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, confirming Hypothesis 1b, with the effect left-lateralized and parietal-occipital-maximal.

Experiment 3 found no pupil-dilation difference between conditions once selection difficulty was equalized, ruling out a structural/difficulty confound for the effects observed in Experiments 1 and 2.
Contrary to Hypothesis 2, pupil dilation and EEG alpha power changes did not correlate in either Experiment 1 or Experiment 2, despite both measures independently registering the load effect.

Alpha power change correlated negatively with LGVT reading-comprehension score in both experiments (marginal in Exp.1, significant in Exp.2), while pupil-dilation change showed no such relationship, interpreted as evidence that alpha power indexes a narrower, more purely cognitive process than pupil dilation.

Two non-adjudicated explanations are offered for the persistent pupil/alpha non-correlation: differential sensitivity to distinct load aspects (cognitive vs. motivational/emotional/arousal), or individual differences in which measure is more sensitive per participant.
The paradigm's ecological validity is limited by non-functional (dead-end) links, forced linear reading, and repeated same-position link sequences unlike naturalistic hypertext browsing.

concepts.term: Executive Functions (EF): updating, shifting, inhibition (Miyake et al.)
locus coeruleus-noradrenergic (LC-NE) arousal account of pupil dilation

interlocutors.name: Kintsch, Walter (1988, 1991) -- construction-integration model
interlocutors.role: theoretical model of text comprehension distinguishing construction (textbase) and integration (situation-model) steps, framing where link-selection load should act

interlocutors.name: Miyake, Akira, Friedman, N.P., Emerson, M.J., Witzki, A.H., & Howerter, A. (2000)
interlocutors.role: unity/diversity of executive functions; source of the updating/shifting/inhibition EF taxonomy adopted throughout

interlocutors.name: Fitzsimmons, G., Weal, M., & Drieghe, D. (2013)
interlocutors.role: only directly comparable prior study isolating link-selection load from subsequent-page load; found no overall disruption effect from non-clickable hyperlinks, motivating this study's extension

interlocutors.name: Kahneman, Daniel, & Beatty, J. (1966)
interlocutors.role: foundational pupillometry study linking pupil diameter to memory/cognitive load

interlocutors.name: Laeng, Bruno, Sirois, S., & Gredeback, G. (2012)
interlocutors.role: locus-coeruleus/arousal account of pupillometry as a broad load measure sensitive to motivation/emotion/arousal

interlocutors.name: Di Stasi, L.L., Antoli, A., Gea, M., & Canas, J.J. (2011)
interlocutors.role: hypermedia pupillometry study finding limited sensitivity of pupil dilation to subjective task difficulty in complex, unconstrained tasks; motivates this study's more tightly controlled paradigm

interlocutors.name: Pfurtscheller, G., & Lopes da Silva, F.H. (1999)
interlocutors.role: event-related desynchronization/synchronization (ERD/ERS) framework underlying the EEG alpha-power analysis

interlocutors.name: Klimesch, Wolfgang (2012, 1999)
interlocutors.role: alpha-band oscillations as an index of attention and controlled access to stored information; theoretical grounding for treating alpha ERD as a cognitive-process marker

interlocutors.name: Antonenko, P., & Niederhauser, D.S. (2010)
interlocutors.role: prior EEG-alpha study of hypertext leads/previews and cognitive load during link selection; closest prior EEG-hypertext precedent, though confounded by perceptual differences

interlocutors.name: Gevins, A., & Smith, M.E. (1997, 2000, 2003)
interlocutors.role: EEG topographic studies establishing parietal electrode sites as representative for alpha-power load effects

interlocutors.name: Duggan, G.B., & Payne, S.J. (2009, 2011); Reader, W.R., & Payne, S.J. (2007)
interlocutors.role: text-skimming and satisficing reading-strategy research, cited in discussing the study's forced-linear-reading ecological-validity limitation

tensions.axis: controlled, artificial laboratory paradigm (non-functional links, forced linear reading) vs. ecological validity of naturalistic hypertext browsing
tensions.note: the authors explicitly acknowledge that their non-functional links, repeated same-position link sequences, and linear-reading instructions may not generalize to genuine, self-directed hypertext browsing, proposing more realistic materials as future work.

tensions.axis: pupil dilation as a broad load/arousal/motivation measure vs. EEG alpha power as a narrower, purely cognitive load measure
tensions.note: the paper's central empirical puzzle: both measures independently track the experimental load manipulation, yet never correlate with each other, and only alpha power (not pupil dilation) correlates with the behavioral comprehension outcome -- left unresolved.

tensions.axis: differential-sensitivity explanation vs. individual-differences explanation for the pupil/alpha non-correlation
tensions.note: two competing post-hoc accounts are offered without adjudication between them, with the authors calling for further combined EEG/eye-tracking research to resolve the question.

dataset_channels.target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study) -- pupillometry channel
dataset_channels.note: Scharinger et al.'s 250 Hz remote infrared eye-tracker protocol (chin-rest-stabilized, 9-point calibration, ~70cm fixed distance) offers a research-grade methodological template for a future VR attention study's pupillometry channel, but a VR headset's built-in eye-tracking would differ substantially in geometry (headset-relative, often lower-resolution) from this screen-based external-sensor setup; linkage requires the dataset entry's own instrumentation to be confirmed (P/anticipatory-application).

dataset_channels.target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study) -- EEG alpha channel
dataset_channels.note: Scharinger et al.'s 27-electrode, 500Hz, ICA-artifact-corrected EEG protocol with a defined alpha-band (8-13Hz) power-extraction procedure at parietal electrode Pz offers a research-grade methodological template for a future VR attention study's EEG channel, but VR headset-integrated EEG (if any) would differ substantially in electrode count/placement and form factor from this full-cap laboratory setup; linkage requires the dataset entry's own instrumentation to be confirmed (P/anticipatory-application).
